newsitem.title: TURKEY: FIRST IRAQI CEYHAN CRUDE LIFTING DELAYED-TERMINAL.
newsitem.headline: FIRST IRAQI CEYHAN CRUDE LIFTING DELAYED-TERMINAL.

text.p: Turkey's Ceyhan oil terminal officials said on Wednesday that the first tanker to lift Iraqi oil under the second term of the oil-for-food deal had not yet begun loadings and was waiting off the port.
"The tanker Arcadia is still waiting off the port and I don't expect any loading today. There seems to be a delay," terminal manager Fatih Sen told Reuters.
Another official said the delay could put forward the first loading "as late as this weekend."
The Arcadia has been waiting off Ceyhan since Monday to lift 2.1 million barrels of Iraqi Kirkuk crude for U.S. trader Bayoil, according to the preliminary lifting schedule.
Iraq plans to sell about 1.5 million barrels per day until September 5, when the first 90-days of the second six-month oil-for-food deal expires.
